title: Étale inverse image: ring lift and hom-set comparison
statement: Let U and V be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and f : U → V any morphism. On their small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let L = Scheme.etaleSetPullback f be the set inverse image [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and assume L preserves finite limits. Let Rr be direct image on commutative-ring-valued sheaves, defined by precomposition with base change, and FrU, FrV the forgetful functors to set sheaves. There exist Lr, an adjunction ar : Lr ⊣ Rr, and a natural isomorphism er : Lr ⋙ FrU ≅ FrV ⋙ L. For all G, F and h : Lr G → F, FrV(ar.homEquiv G F h) = a.homEquiv (FrV G) (FrU F) (er_G⁻¹ ≫ FrU(h)), where a is the set adjunction. For every G there are source and target sheaf morphisms representing sectionwise addition, zero, negation, multiplication and one. Each binary operation op satisfies L(opV) = prodComparison L ≫ prod.map er_G⁻¹ er_G⁻¹ ≫ opU ≫ er_G; each constant c satisfies L(cV) = terminal.from _ ≫ cU ≫ er_G; negation satisfies L(negV) = er_G⁻¹ ≫ negU ≫ er_G. All section formulas use the chosen product projections and chosen terminal sheaves. No unit compatibility or abelian inverse-image comparison is assumed in this lemma.

source.place: Proposition 00YV, proof of (2) and its paragraph on rings; discussion of quadruples and sextuples in Section 00YR

proof.text: Obtain Lr, ar, er and the forgetful hom-set identity from the ring-sheaf adjunction construction. No operation transport equations are taken from that statement.

For a ring sheaf on either site, define addition and multiplication using the chosen product projections; define zero and one as constant natural transformations from the chosen terminal sheaf and negation sectionwise. Naturality of the projections and preservation of the five operations by restriction ring homomorphisms prove naturality of all these maps. Their section formulas hold by definition.

Evaluate the forgetful hom-set identity at the identity of Lr(G). The image of ar.unit(G) is the set unit followed by the set direct image of er(G) inverse. To prove each transport formula, compose both sides with er(G) inverse and apply injectivity of the set adjunction bijection. Its formula using the unit, unit naturality, and the preceding identity reduce the unary and constant equations to the sectionwise preservation of negation, zero and one by ar.unit(G).

For the binary formulas let q be the left product comparison followed by the product of the two inverse components of er, and let t be its adjunct. The product comparison projection equations and unit naturality show that t followed by the direct image of either target projection equals the corresponding source projection followed by the underlying ar.unit(G). Evaluate these two equalities on sections, substitute into the target binary operation, and use preservation of addition or multiplication by the ring homomorphism ar.unit(G). Injectivity of the adjunction bijection and cancellation of er(G) inverse give exactly the two required transport equations.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 00YV, ring paragraph; operation formulas deduced by adjunct injectivity and the ring-valued unit.
